answer_1.quote: We present TACT, a dataset for modeling the integration of task-oriented and chitchat dialogues with natural mode transitions and recoverable structures. TACT enables training models that can manage complex dialogue flows, including multi-turn mode shifts and returns to prior tasks.
answer_1.outputs: The outputs are conversational responses in multi-turn dialogues that alternate between task-oriented and chitchat modes, with an emphasis on smooth transitions and recovery to prior tasks.

answer_2.quote: We use three metrics to assess a model's task-handling abilities. (1) Mode Selection Accuracy and F1... (2) Intent Detection Accuracy... (3) Mode+Intent Joint Accuracy...

answer_3.quote: The judging model, GPT-4O-MINI scores each dialogue on three criteria: (1) Intent Accuracy, which checks whether the user intent is correctly conveyed and executed; (2) Transition Quality, which assesses whether mode switches are contextually justified; and (3) Dialogue Naturalness, which evaluates fluency and coherence.

answer_4.quote: The human study was conducted on a 77-sample subset of the test set, where annotators evaluated responses without a tie option, providing an additional perspective aligned with real user interactions (Figure ).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were provided with a short guideline and a dedicated web interface. The instruction included evaluation criteria such as whether the response makes sense, is specific, is interesting, and whether the transition is natural.
